# New renderings — iliad-103 (16.394–476)

Format as the house table: Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀπετίνυτο ποινήν (16.398) | "exacted requital" | "took requital" | "took vengeance" (reserved for τίνομαι), "exacted a price"; ποινή "requital" as in the table (3.290); the genitive πολέων is "for many" |
| ἐπέκερσε φάλαγγας (16.394) | "had cut off … battle-lines" | "had cut off the foremost battle-lines" | "mown down", "sheared through"; φάλαγξ "battle-line" (3.77) |
| παλιμπετές (16.395) | "backward" | "driving them backward" (+ note: formation uncertain) | "in flight", "headlong back"; adverb from πάλιν + a root "fall/fly", not certain |
| ἱερὸν ἰχθύν (16.407) | "a sacred fish" | "a sacred fish" (+ note: why a fish is "sacred" is not known) | "a great fish", "a living fish", "a lively fish"; ἱερός "sacred" as in the table (1.366) |
| ἤνοπι χαλκῷ (16.408) | "gleaming bronze" | "gleaming bronze" (+ note: sense of ἤνοψ uncertain, traditional gloss) | "shining" (reserved for φαεινός), "bright", "flashing"; no derivation claimed |
| θύραζε (16.408) | "to the outside" | "onto the land" | "to the door", "ashore"; the -ζε ending is "to" |

| βριαρῇ (κόρυθι, 16.413) | "weighty" | "heavy" | "strong", "stout" (kept for παχύς), "sturdy"; follows the table’s βριαρός (11.375) "weighty" / "heavy" |
| μέσσην κὰκ κεφαλήν (16.411–412) | "down on the middle of the head" | "in the middle of the head" | "right on the head", "full on the head" (drop μέσσην); μέσση "middle" as at iliad-082 (13.506) |
| ἄνδιχα … κεάσθη (16.412) | "was split in two" | "was split in two" | "cleft", "was shattered"; κεάζω "split" |

## Departures and reuse

- 16.443 (ἔρδ’ here, ἕρδ’ in iliad-021) takes the published English of that line; 16.457 takes the English of odyssey-117 (i: "the prize of honour that belongs to the dead").
- 16.439, 16.440, 16.444, 16.458 are whole units whose Greek is a published Iliad unit's; `l` and `i` are the published ones word for word (440 keeps its opening quotation mark, which is where Hera's speech begins here). 16.426 likewise (iliad-025), 16.401 (iliad-081).
- 16.400 (iliad-102, with Menelaus and Thoas), 16.418 (iliad-048), 16.424–425 (iliad-028), 16.462 (iliad-016) and 16.469 (odyssey-046) occur inside longer or differently cut units of mine; their English is reused word for word as far as the new sentence allows (only the person of the pronoun, tense or closing punctuation change). 16.473 (odyssey-049) changes "my" to "his".
- No departure from the Odyssey table in any epithet or formula. The one place a table row had two competing forms, εὐρείης of Lycia, follows the shipped "wide Lycia" (iliad-037) and not the row "broad" for places.
- Quotation marks: Sarpedon 422–425 opens with “ at 422 and closes with ” at 425; Zeus 433–438 opens at 433 and closes at 438; Hera 440–457 opens at 440 and closes at 457 (3 opening and 3 closing marks in each layer).
